prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the right attorney depends on the facts of your crash, the severity of injuries, whether fault is disputed, and your priorities (highest recovery vs. quick settlement vs. trial experience). I can help you find someone great for your situation — below are practical steps, a few reputable Chicago firms that handle serious car-accident claims, and what to ask at consults.

Reputable Chicago firms that handle car-accident/personal-injury cases
- Clifford Law Offices — large plaintiff firm with experience in catastrophic auto cases and high-value recoveries.  
- Corboy & Demetrio — long history of high-profile personal-injury verdicts and settlements.  
- Levin & Perconti — known for catastrophic injury and wrongful-death auto cases.  
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard — handles auto collisions and serious injury claims.  
- Brown & Crouppen — focuses on auto accidents and serious personal-injury matters.

(These are examples of well-known Chicago plaintiff firms — they’re not guarantees. Use the selection tips below.)

How to pick the best attorney for you
- Experience with car-accident cases similar to yours (neck/back soft-tissue vs. catastrophic injury vs. wrongful death).  
- Trial experience and track record of verdicts and settlements.  
- Client reviews and peer ratings (Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, Google).  
- Resources and staff (do they have investigators, medical experts, trial attorneys?).  
- Communication: who will handle the case day-to-day and how quickly they respond.  
- Fee structure (contingency % and who pays case costs if you don’t recover).  
- Willingness to take case to trial if insurer offers too little.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the results?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? Will it be an associate?  
- What is your contingency fee and what costs are deducted from a recovery?  
- Do you expect this to settle or go to trial?  
- What is a realistic range for recovery in my situation and why?  
- Do you have any disciplinary history? (You can also check IL ARDC: https://www.iardc.org/)

What to bring to an initial consult
- Police report, photos of damage/injuries, medical records/bills, insurance information (yours and other driver’s), employer info (lost wages), witness info, and a short timeline of events.

Practical notes
- Illinois statute of limitations for personal injury from a car crash is generally 2 years from the date of the accident (act promptly).  
- Most personal-injury lawyers in Illinois work on contingency (commonly ~33% if settled pre-suit; higher if case goes to trial). Confirm specifics with each firm.

If you’d like, tell me:
- your ZIP code, a short summary of the crash (date, injuries, fault/dispute, insurance limits), and whether you want maximum recovery or a quick resolution — and I’ll shortlist attorneys in Chicago who are a good match and show recent client reviews and contact options.
